notes.detailedSummary: Proves the Plucker annihilator obstruction on Lambda^2 R^4, reconstructs the four foundational 369 items on the same ordinary open with q=n-p and r=q-1, repairs printed sign/index/cone problems, and preserves nonreduced integration weights. Imports precisely recorded standard CLD/analytic foundations. The 6561-pair diagnostic is finite evidence, not an analytic proof.
notes.text:
# Ordinary calculus, positivity, and exact integration weights

This is an independent mathematical draft. Fix a complete non-Archimedean field \(K\), with trivial valuation permitted, a good separated strict boundaryless pure \(n\)-dimensional analytic space \(X\), \(n\geq2\), and an ordinary open \(N\subset X\). Put \(D=d'd''\). A positive current means a symmetric current nonnegative on middle-positive complementary tests, as in CLD 7.2.1. If \(T\) has bidegree \((p,p)\), put \(q=n-p\) and \(r=q-1\). Tests for \(T\) have type \((q,q)\); tests for \(D(hT)\) have type \((r,r)\). All products and tests below are ordinary CLD products and ordinary smooth tests on the indicated open.

The primary reference is Chambert-Loir--Ducros, Formes differentielles reelles et courants sur les espaces de Berkovich, arXiv:1204.6277v2, retained cover 25 July 2025, internal title 29 July 2025, 0h06. Its complete applied statements and immediate proofs were displayed in 31 bounded units. The complete book was retained, not read page by page. The ledger states the imported recursive analytic and measure-theoretic foundations. Previous note bodies, reading records, PASS labels, and ROOT decisions are data, not premises.

The needed primary statements are these. CLD 11.1.7 gives compact neighborhood bases, affinoid neighborhood bases on good spaces, and the analytic-domain structure of ordinary opens. CLD 15.7.1--2 supplies the canonical calibrated level-\(n\) calculus and its analytic-domain restriction for topologically separated pure analytic spaces. CLD 15.2.2--4 proves local differential separation for good separated spaces by separating seminorms with an analytic function, composing its logarithmic norm with a real smooth separator, and extending by zero near its zeros. CLD 6.2.4--8 and 15.2.5--9 gives compact smooth plateaus in prescribed opens, compact scalar density, and finite localization on compact supports. No global paracompactness of \(N\) is assumed. These inputs have no reducedness or nontrivial-valuation assumption.

For clarity, finite nonnegative localization follows directly from these plateau results. Cover a compact set by finitely many relatively compact smaller neighborhoods inside the proposed chart opens, choose nonnegative plateaus on them, and divide their sum into each plateau where the sum is positive. Multiply by a further plateau supported where the sum is positive and equal to one near the compact set. The resulting finite smooth functions sum to one near that set and have compact supports inside the specified opens. Uniform approximation of continuous compact scalars follows from real Stone--Weierstrass on the one-point compactification, followed by multiplication by a prescribed-open plateau. These are uses of scalar density, not pluriharmonic regularization.

There is an essential cone distinction. On a real vector space \(E\), let \(\sigma_a=(-1)^{a(a-1)/2}\). A symmetric \((a,a)\)-form is middle-positive exactly when its coefficient matrix in the convention \(\sigma_a\xi_I\wedge J\xi_J\) is PSD; this is CLD 1.2.6. For \(\lambda=\sum_i d's_i\wedge d''s_i\),
\[
 \lambda^a=a!\sigma_a\sum_{|I|=a}d's_I\wedge J(d's_I).
\]
Thus its matrix is a positive scalar multiple of the identity on the actual \(a\)-th exterior coefficient space. It dominates both signs of every bounded symmetric coefficient matrix. Pullback and wedge preserve middle positivity by CLD 1.2.11--12. The size of this coefficient space is determined by the moment chart, not by the analytic dimension.

Strong-positive domination of all symmetric middle-degree forms is false. In \(\Lambda^2\mathbb R^4\), use the ordered coordinates \(12,13,14,23,24,34\). For \(w=a\wedge b\), the coefficient of \(w\wedge w=0\) is twice
\[
 P(w)=w_{12}w_{34}-w_{13}w_{24}+w_{14}w_{23}=0.
\]
The corresponding linear functional \(L(B)=B_{12,34}-B_{13,24}+B_{14,23}\) vanishes on the span of all decomposable-square generators of the strong-positive cone. It vanishes on the diagonal matrix representing \(\lambda^2\). But \(L(vv^t)=1\) for \(v=e_{12}+e_{34}\). Consequently neither \(c\lambda^2+vv^t\) nor \(c\lambda^2-vv^t\) can be strongly positive for any \(c\). Middle PSD domination remains valid. This proves, rather than merely diagnoses by computation, the needed correction to 367/368 and to the printed strong-domination step in CLD 7.2.9. The retained page 162 pixels confirm that this word occurs in the PDF; CLD 1.2.13 itself states only relative interior for the strong cone. We import no general recognition theorem for arbitrary weakly positive functionals.

Here are the four basic calculus conclusions of 369, with their complete arguments.

First, if a compact symmetric \((q,q)\)-form \(\beta\) on \(N\) has support inside an ordinary \(O\subset N\), then
\[
 \beta=\eta_+-\eta_-,\qquad\eta_\pm\in\mathcal A_c^{q,q}(O),\quad\eta_\pm\geq0.
\]
CLD 6.5.2 applies on \(O\) itself: compact analytic supports on almost-good spaces satisfy its support condition, and good ordinary domains are almost good. Its finite chart proof can also be reconstructed by the preceding localization, middle PSD domination on compact chart images, and summation. Compact outputs extend smoothly by zero to Hausdorff \(N\). They can have larger support than \(\beta\), but stay in \(O\). The compact constant-majorant argument suffices; the erroneous noncompact majorant/composition wording in CLD 1.10.2 is unused.

Second, for each compact diagonal test \(\theta\) complementary to positive \(T\), there is a unique finite signed Radon measure \(\mu_{T,\theta}\), supported in \(\operatorname{supp}\theta\), with
\[
 \int f\,d\mu_{T,\theta}=\langle T,f\theta\rangle
\]
for compact smooth scalars \(f\). For a positive test, CLD 7.2.8 and 7.2.11 gives the positive measure: bound a scalar by its supremum times a nonnegative plateau and extend by scalar density. For general \(\theta\), discard its antisymmetric part and subtract the measures of the preceding middle-positive decomposition. Scalar density gives uniqueness and independence of decomposition. On the complement of \(\operatorname{supp}\theta\), the smooth scalar functional is zero; density there proves the stated support, even if decomposition enlarged the supports. The ordinary multiplication of CLD 7.2.12 therefore satisfies
\[
 \langle bT,\theta\rangle=\int b\,d\mu_{T,\theta},\qquad
 |\langle bT,\theta\rangle|\leq\sup_{\operatorname{supp}\theta}|b|\,|\mu_{T,\theta}|(N).
\]
The repaired order-zero justification uses only the middle cone: on each compact chart image the standard power dominates both signs of a test by a constant times its coefficient norm, cellwise in a finite subdivision; finite localization bounds the functional in the chart \(C^0\) topology. This is the printed 7.2.9 argument with middle positivity throughout, valid for the given middle-positive \(T\). It also shows the locally bounded scalar multiplier is a current in the same calculus.

For \(\beta=\eta_+-\eta_-\) and \(\eta=\eta_++\eta_-\), positivity and uniqueness give the particularly useful bound
\[
 |\langle bT,\beta\rangle|
 \leq\int |b|\,d\mu_{T,\eta}
 \leq\sup_{\operatorname{supp}\eta}|b|\,\langle T,\eta\rangle.                 \tag{1}
\]
The mass is identified by a smooth scalar equal to one on the compact supports. For fixed \(T\), locally uniform convergence \(b_i\to b\) consequently gives \(b_iT\to bT\) on every fixed compact test. No changing-current assertion has been inferred.

Third, for ordinary smooth \(g\) and doubly closed positive \(T\),
\[
 D(gT)=Dg\wedge T.                                                        \tag{2}
\]
On a compact symmetric \((r,r)\)-test \(\alpha\), set \(A=g\,d''\alpha-d''g\wedge\alpha\), of type \((q-1,q)\). Total-degree Leibniz gives
\[
 Dg\wedge\alpha-gD\alpha=-d'A+C,\qquad
 C=d'g\wedge d''\alpha+d''g\wedge d'\alpha.
\]
The identities \(Jd'=d''J\), \(Jd''=-d'J\) give \(JC=-C\). Symmetry of \(T\) kills \(C\), and \(d'T=0\) kills \(d'A\). Signed transposition gives \(\langle DS,\alpha\rangle=\langle S,D\alpha\rangle\), proving (2). Both currents are symmetric, so symmetric tests suffice. Both closedness equations are retained. This replaces the misindexed printed CLD 8.5.3 and 7.7.5 statements by correctly typed direct arguments.

Fourth, if \(Z\subset N\) is ordinary closed and continuous \(h\) is ordinary smooth with \(Dh=0\) on \(N\setminus Z\), then \(R=D(hT)\) is symmetric, supported in \(Z\). Equation (2), restriction, and CLD 7.1.9 proves this. If \(\chi=1\) near \(Z\cap\operatorname{supp}\alpha\), then
\[
 \langle R,\alpha\rangle=\langle R,\chi\alpha\rangle.                      \tag{3}
\]
The compact support of \((1-\chi)\alpha\) misses \(Z\). No order-zero or positivity assertion is needed for \(R\). The same support conclusion holds if, off \(Z\), \(h\) is locally a uniform limit on compact sets of ordinary smooth \(g_i\) with \(Dg_i=0\): (2), fixed-\(T\) continuity, and transposition makes \(D(hT)=0\) there.

All exterior signs use total degree. Moving a type \((a,b)\)-form across a type \((c,d)\)-form gives \((-1)^{(a+b)(c+d)}\), directly by permuting exterior generators and consistently with CLD 1.3.3. The different exponent printed in 3.3.10 is confirmed in the retained page 80 pixels. Also the \(d_K\) in the proof of 3.3.6 must be \(d_{\rm trop}\), as its statement and ensuing argument show. These are explicit algebraic repairs, not permission to change the underlying calculus.

We will also use the exact analytic support statement CLD 15.2.1: a type \((a,b)\) G-form on a topologically separated analytic space has support in \(d_K(x)\geq\max(a,b)\); its support misses a locally Zariski-closed analytic locus \(Y\) of dimension below \(\max(a,b)\). Ordinary forms are G-forms. The immediate proof uses \(d_{\rm trop}(x)\leq d_K(x)\) from 12.4.2, form vanishing in insufficient tropical dimension from 3.3.6, and \(d_K(y)\leq\dim Y\) from analytic dimension theory. Here \(d_K\) is graded residual transcendence degree, equivalently residue-field transcendence degree plus rational value-group rank. A projected skeleton dimension is not a substitute.

Finally, the integration weights are the original ones. For an Artinian local ring \(A\), CLD 13.3.4 uses \(\delta_A(B)=\ell_A(B)/\ell_A(A)\). A composition-series calculation gives multiplicativity through finite local algebras. CLD 13.3.7 sums the finite local fiber modules, giving calibrated degree \(\lambda/\mu\) when the generic module length is \(\lambda\) and the base generic Artinian length is \(\mu\); nilreduction has degree \(1/\mu\). CLD 14.4.2 transports the canonical calibration by this degree; 15.4.2--3 then transports top-form integration. Since top-form supports avoid lower-dimensional component intersections, 16.6.3 gives
\[
 \delta_X=\sum_i m_i\delta_{X_{i,\mathrm{red}}}
\]
with actual generic lengths \(m_i\). The calibration is independent under appending analytic units by its common-moment construction in 14.3.1--5. No normalization or base extension of the arbitrary \(T\) is performed. Boundaryless Stokes gives both closedness equations for \(\delta_X\). Its BT property is tautological because \(h\delta_X=[h]\).

The universal identity was proved by exterior algebra above. Source integrity and successful execution do not establish mathematical correctness.

notes.detailedSummary: Proves weighted cutoff estimates and their exact vanishing criterion, test-specific mass infima and inverse-oscillation lower bounds, ordinary cover localization, removal for dim Z<n-p-1, and the necessary analytic detector bound d_K>=n-p-1. Off-locus regularity and the analytic-locus hypotheses remain explicit; the dimensional window supplies no counterexample.
notes.text:
# All cutoff and dimension conclusions of 369

Use the four calculus lemmas proved in local note n1, on one fixed ordinary open \(N\), with positive doubly closed \(T\), \(q=n-p\), and \(r=q-1\). Let \(Z\subset N\) be ordinary closed and \(h\) continuous, ordinary smooth with zero smooth Hessian off \(Z\). The six following arguments complete the ten-item chain of 369.

Fix a compact symmetric \((r,r)\)-test \(\alpha\), and put \(S=Z\cap\operatorname{supp}\alpha\). For any ordinary neighborhood \(O\) of \(S\), choose \(0\leq\chi\leq1\) compact smooth in \(O\), equal to one near \(S\). Decompose, on \(O\) itself,
\[
 D(\chi\alpha)=\eta_+-\eta_-,\qquad\eta=\eta_++\eta_-,\quad\eta_\pm\geq0.
\]
For a smooth \(g\) on the same \(N\) with \(Dg=0\), n1's support localization, transposition, and smooth multiplier identity gives
\[
 \langle D(hT),\alpha\rangle
 =\langle (h-g)T,D(\chi\alpha)\rangle,
\]
and hence
\[
 |\langle D(hT),\alpha\rangle|
 \leq\int|h-g|\,d\mu_{T,\eta}
 \leq\sup_{\operatorname{supp}\eta}|h-g|\,\langle T,\eta\rangle.              \tag{4}
\]
Subtracting \(g\) is legitimate because \(D(gT)=0\), even though \(hT\) need not be closed. These are actual upstairs tests with compact positive outputs in the specified \(O\). For empty \(S\), take all cutoff forms zero. This proves item 5.

If, for each \(\alpha\), actual triples \((\chi_j,\eta_{j,\pm},g_j)\) on the same \(N\) make the integral in (4) tend to zero, then the fixed left pairing is zero. All symmetric tests determine the symmetric defect, so \(D(hT)=0\). The vanishing of supremum error times mass is a sufficient stronger premise. The functions \(g_j\) need only approximate \(h\) on the moving supports, not on all of \(N\). This proves item 6 without assuming the existence of such triples for an arbitrary pair.

Define \(\mathcal C_{T,\alpha}(S;O)\) as the infimum of \(\langle T,\eta_++\eta_-\rangle\) over precisely the actual cutoff/decomposition competitors above. A competitor exists, its mass is finite, and positivity gives a nonnegative infimum. It is zero for empty \(S\), and nondecreasing as \(O\) shrinks. For relatively compact \(O\), let \(\omega_g(O)=\sup_O|h-g|\). Taking the infimum in (4), without assuming attainment, gives
\[
 |\langle D(hT),\alpha\rangle|\leq
 \omega_g(O)\mathcal C_{T,\alpha}(S;O).                                    \tag{5}
\]
If \(h=g\) on compact \(S\), continuity gives relatively compact neighborhoods with arbitrarily small \(\omega_g\). Uniformly bounded cutoff masses, or merely a vanishing product in (5), proves removability. Conversely a detector of magnitude \(d>0\) forces \(\mathcal C\geq d/\omega_g\) where \(\omega_g>0\), and forbids \(\omega_g=0\). This proves item 7. Separate finite masses on each neighborhood do not imply uniformly bounded masses. This quantity is test-specific; it is not identified with a standard capacity.

If these estimates establish zero on members of an ordinary cover of a specified \(W\), then ordinary restriction and finite nonnegative localization of compact tests makes the same current zero on \(W\). This proves item 8. It glues established identities for the original current; it does not construct closed approximating currents by a partition. A cover of \(W\) is not a basis inside every ordinary open.

Suppose now \(Z\) is locally Zariski closed in analytic domains, with \(\dim Z<r=n-p-1\). The exact CLD support theorem stated and checked in n1 makes every compact \((r,r)\)-test support disjoint from \(Z\). The defect is supported in \(Z\), so all its pairings vanish. Ordinary localization proves \(D(hT)=0\), which is item 9. The same proof works for ordinary closed \(Z\) with the actual pointwise condition \(d_K(z)<r\). For a pure codimension \(c\), the integer bound is \(c\geq p+2\). When \(p=n-1\), \(r=0\); this method removes no nonempty locus.

For item 10, a nonzero defect has a compact detecting test by definition. Symmetrize it. Its support must meet \(Z\), and every point of its support has \(d_K\geq r\). Thus a detector meets \(Z\) at an actual analytic point with \(d_K\geq n-p-1\). Applying item 9 to the original \(\delta_X\) gives \(D[h]=0\) if \(\dim Z<n-1\), with the actual Artinian weights retained. This does not recognize either sign of \(h\) as psh or furnish individually admissible \(U,V\). For \(p\geq1\), the inequalities \(n-p-1\leq\dim Z<n-1\) leave a dimensional window unexcluded by this method. They do not exhibit a counterexample. At \(p=0\) there is no such window.

These ten statements are conditional partial results. The whole369 paper and proof, all three actual FINAL texts, and all three distinct expanded texts were examined as different artifacts. The independently reconstructed results use n1's middle-cone, sign, and degree repairs. No universal off-locus regularity, trace geometry, or weighted vanishing follows here from \(D[h]=0\).

notes.detailedSummary: Proves continuous multiplication compatibility via signed coefficient measures, the full graded D(gamma hT) formula and both cross relations, every-open relative transfer, fixed-T scalar nets, and common-chart coefficient limits to smooth factors. Gives an actual torus detector showing a positive scalar can destroy closedness; that current is ineligible for original P21.3.
notes.text:
# Complete scalar and smooth-form factor transfer

Use n1's signed coefficient measures and ordinary scalar products. Let \(\mathcal F(O)\subset C(O,\mathbb R)\) be any prescribed restriction-compatible class of finite functions. A positive doubly closed current \(T\) is BT for \(\mathcal F\) if, on every ordinary \(O\), all \(u,v\in\mathcal F(O)\) with \(D[u]=D[v]\) have \(D((u-v)T)=0\). Initial BT is an explicit hypothesis in the transfer statements below. The original individually continuous psh class can be used without replacing it by generated CPsh.

For a smooth form \(\beta\) and a complementary compact test \(\omega\), \(\beta\wedge\omega\) has the complementary diagonal type for \(T\). Since \(T\) has even total degree, n1 gives
\[
 \langle\beta\wedge(hT),\omega\rangle
 =\int h\,d\mu_{T,\beta\wedge\omega}.                                    \tag{6}
\]
If \(\beta\wedge T=0\), evaluate that zero current on \(f\omega\) for all smooth scalars \(f\). Measure uniqueness makes the measure in (6) zero, proving \(\beta\wedge(hT)=0\). For a smooth scalar \(a\), uniqueness gives \(\mu_{T,a\theta}=a\mu_{T,\theta}\), hence \(a(hT)=(ah)T\). For positive \(C=\gamma\wedge T\), its coefficient measure agrees with \(\mu_{T,\gamma\wedge\omega}\) on every smooth scalar, so
\[
 hC=\gamma\wedge(hT).                                                     \tag{7}
\]
For continuous \(a\geq0\), the same uniqueness applied to the ordinary positive \(aT\) gives \(h(aT)=(ha)T\). These statements use the measures of positive \(T\); they invent no continuous wedge on an arbitrary signed current.

For any current \(S\) and smooth \(\beta\) of total degree \(b\), signed transposition and total-degree exterior commutation proves
\[
 d(\beta\wedge S)=d\beta\wedge S+(-1)^b\beta\wedge dS,\qquad d=d',d''.
\]
Indeed move \(\beta\) past total-degree-\(m\) \(S\) with \((-1)^{bm}\), transpose the differential with \((-1)^{m+b+1}\), and expand \(d(\beta\wedge\omega)\) on each compact test. The two resulting signs are exactly the displayed terms. This is also the correctly indexed argument of CLD 7.7.7. No closedness of \(S\) is assumed. For smooth \((k,k)\)-form \(\gamma\), applying both rules gives
\[
 D(\gamma\wedge S)=D\gamma\wedge S-d''\gamma\wedge d'S
                  +d'\gamma\wedge d''S+\gamma\wedge DS.                  \tag{8}
\]

Suppose \(T\) and \(C=\gamma\wedge T\) are doubly closed. First-order Leibniz gives \(d'\gamma\wedge T=d''\gamma\wedge T=0\). Differentiating the second gives \(D\gamma\wedge T=0\). Put \(S=hT\). The measure argument inherits all three annihilators for \(S\). Differentiate the first by \(d''\) and the second by \(d'\), remembering that both differentiated form factors have odd total degree:
\[
 0=-D\gamma\wedge S-d'\gamma\wedge d''S,
 \qquad0=D\gamma\wedge S-d''\gamma\wedge d'S.
\]
Thus both cross terms in (8), as well as its \(D\gamma\) term, vanish. We obtain
\[
 D(\gamma\wedge(hT))=\gamma\wedge D(hT).                                  \tag{9}
\]
This calculation keeps \(S=hT\) potentially nonclosed. For a scalar factor it reads \(D((ah)T)=aD(hT)\) under closedness of \(aT\).

Consequently, for an initial BT current \(T\), an actual smooth-factor product \(C=\gamma\wedge T\) is BT if and only if it is positive and doubly closed. Necessity is in the definition. For sufficiency restrict to arbitrary ordinary \(O\), take an admissible pair there, put \(h=u-v\), and apply initial \(D(hT)=0\), (7), and (9). The form \(\gamma\) itself need be neither positive nor closed. Its actual product must be positive, and closedness is precisely \(d'\gamma\wedge T=d''\gamma\wedge T=0\). The degree range is \(p+k\leq n\); original nontrivial P21.3 tests require \(p+k\leq n-1\), while degree \(n\) has no Hessian tests. In particular a smooth \(a\geq0\) is allowable exactly when \(aT\) is doubly closed.

The fixed-current scalar-net theorem is equally exact. If locally smooth \(a_i\geq0\) converge locally uniformly to continuous \(a\), and EACH \(a_iT\) is doubly closed for the FIXED initial BT \(T\), then \(aT\) is positive and closed by n1's coefficient-measure convergence and transposition. For any admissible \(h\) on any ordinary subopen and compact detecting \(\omega\),
\[
 \langle D((a_i-a)hT),\omega\rangle
 =\int(a_i-a)h\,d\mu_{T,D\omega}\longrightarrow0.
\]
The measure is finite and \(h\) bounded on its compact support. Each earlier identity is zero, giving BT in the limit; ordinary locality completes the every-open statement. Unrestricted smooth approximation supplies none of the required closedness equations.

For the form-net version, assume EACH smooth \(\gamma_i\wedge T\) positive and doubly closed, and convergence in coefficients on compact supports in a FIXED finite family of common moment charts to a SMOOTH \(\gamma\). Localize a test and expand the factors in the finite exterior monomial bases. Each monomial times the localized test has a fixed finite signed coefficient measure of \(T\). Uniform coefficient convergence proves weak convergence of the products. Apply the same argument to \(d'\omega,d''\omega\) to get closedness, and pass on positive tests to get positivity. For BT use \(D\omega\) and multiply converging coefficients by the fixed bounded \(h\), then use (7). This produces no nonsmooth wedge, changing-chart convergence theorem, or density of arbitrary currents.

The complete source-scope diagnostic is analytic. On \(X=(\mathbb G_{m,\mathbb Q_\ell}^2)^{\rm an}\), let \(s_i=-\log|T_i|\) and \(a=2+s_1^2>0\). This is good separated strict boundaryless pure dimension two. Its \(\delta_X\) is positive, doubly closed, and tautologically BT. However
\[
 D(a\delta_X)=[2d's_1\wedge d''s_1].
\]
For nonzero \(\zeta\geq0\) smooth compact on \(\mathbb R^2\), the actual test \(\omega=\zeta(s)d's_2\wedge d''s_2\) has compact support in a closed analytic polyannulus. The identity moment has finite-flat degree one; CLD 14.3.1--5, 14.5.2--3 and 5.8.4 gives its standard calibration, with the paired positive orientation. Therefore
\[
 \langle D(a\delta_X),\omega\rangle=2\int_{\mathbb R^2}\zeta(s)\,ds_1ds_2>0.
\]
Thus \(a\delta_X\) is ineligible as a P21.3 current. This diagnoses the absent closedness premise of literal CLD 8.6.7; it is not an original counterexample. Conversely \(S=(d's_1\wedge d''s_1)\wedge\delta_X\) is positive closed BT, and both \(d'a\wedge S,d''a\wedge S\) vanish by repeated generators, so \(aS\) is closed BT. Nonconstant relative weights are allowed.

The entire scalar367 and relative368 statements are proved after replacing their unsupported strong-cone step by n1's middle-cone construction. Their submitted proofs require that correction. The repaired whole372 transfer chain retains initial BT, actual product positivity and double closedness, every approximant's equations, and the smooth form limit. notes.text:
# Analytic-trace removability, the whole372 verdict, and the original decision

The independently reconstructed partial theorem is as follows. Work in the original ambient category of n1. Let \(Z\subset W\) be ordinary closed and locally Zariski closed in analytic domains. Suppose \(h\in C(W,\mathbb R)\) is ordinary smooth with zero smooth Hessian on \(W\setminus Z\). Suppose each point of \(Z\) has an ordinary neighborhood \(N\) and ordinary smooth \(g\) there with \(Dg=0\) and \(h=g\) on \(Z\cap N\). Then \(D(hT)=0\) for EVERY positive doubly closed ordinary \((p,p)\)-current, \(0\leq p\leq n-1\). There is no dimension bound and no assumed cutoff mass bound. The same conclusion holds if off \(Z\) smooth harmonicity is replaced by local uniform-on-compact approximation by ordinary smooth zero-Hessian functions: n1 proves the identical defect-support premise needed below. This small extension retains the substantial approximation and analytic-trace assumptions. It is not original P21.3 closure.

Here is a full construction of the cutoff certificates. Localize inside an affinoid neighborhood and choose a relatively compact ordinary subopen \(N\) carrying the trace \(g\). Affinoid noetherianity supplies analytic \(f_1,\ldots,f_m\) whose common zero set in \(N\) is \(Z\cap N\). The affinoid neighborhood is contained in a domain on which the analytic-locus description is valid. Choose a real \(A\) at least two greater than the upper bounds for their finite logarithmic norms. Real constants avoid any use of nontrivial field scaling.

Let \(R_m\) be convolution of \(\max(s_1,\ldots,s_m)\) with a product of nonnegative smooth probability kernels supported in \([-1/4,1/4]\). It is smooth convex, translation-equivariant in the all-ones direction, and differs from the maximum by at most \(1/4\). If \(s_i\) is at least one below the largest other coordinate, then even after every translation in the kernel support it cannot attain the maximum: the gap stays at least \(1/2\). Integrating out that coordinate omits it exactly. Repeated omission permits coordinates equal to \(-\infty\). In particular near a zero of one \(f_i\) outside the common zero locus, its coordinate is inactive, and the remaining active functions are actual analytic units after ordinary shrinking.

Define off \(Z\)
\[
 t=A-R_m(\log|f_1|,\ldots,\log|f_m|).
\]
CLD 15.1.1--2, as checked in n1's source ledger, makes this an ordinary smooth function on actual unit-moment charts. Its smooth Hessian is nonpositive: the logarithmic-unit functions are affine in those charts and the Hessian of \(R_m\) is PSD. We have \(t\geq0\), and \(t\to+\infty\) at \(Z\).
